decisions.reason: As a broad dietary-supplement line it is only moderately related to the firm's core pharmaceutical knowledge, and with only early web presence and little visible evidence of sustained traction, management would likely reallocate resources away from it.

This skin-and-hair supplement is adjacent to the firm's pharmacy-channel and formulation capabilities, and its dedicated launch and continued 2019 presence suggest enough scope for incremental learning to justify keeping it.

A joint-health supplement fits reasonably well with the firm's existing health-product knowledge and pharmacy distribution, and the move from a mention in 2018 to its own page in 2019 indicates learnable market potential.

The mushroom-based immune supplement is more weakly connected to the firm's established pharmaceutical knowledge base and more exposed to fad-like demand, so absorptive-capacity logic favors dropping it if performance is not clearly strong.

A generic blood-pressure medicine sits squarely inside the firm's core regulatory, manufacturing, and therapeutic expertise, and even with the 2018 valsartan problem the firm is well placed to absorb the issue and continue the product.

An over-the-counter migraine triptan is closely related to the firm's pharmaceutical know-how and pharmacy-market experience, so management would likely keep it and build on existing capabilities rather than exit quickly.
